- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Mental health services would receive investment to achieve parity with physical health, including counsellors in all schools. A National Cancer Control Plan and measures to end new HIV cases by 2030 are included.

## Social Care
The manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment in social care, introducing free personal care modelled on Scotland's system, establishing national pay structures for care workers, and ending exploitation of overseas care workers.

## Housing
Proposals include building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy
The party would halt new fossil fuel extraction, cancel recent licences like Rosebank, and end fossil fuel subsidies. Targets include wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030, with 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore wind, and 100GW solar by 2035. Community ownership of energy infrastructure would be mandated. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy and Work
A £40bn annual green investment programme is proposed, alongside bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. A £15/hour minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and restoration of trade union rights are included. The party would move towards a four-day working week.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, disability benefits would rise 5%, and the bedroom tax would be scrapped. Long-term plans include Universal Basic Income.

## Taxation
Proposals include a wealth tax (1% on assets over £10m, 2% over £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and a carbon tax starting at £120/tonne rising to £500/tonne. The party estimates raising £50-70bn annually from personal tax reforms and up to £80bn from carbon taxes by parliament's end.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would grant legal personhood to nature. Targets include protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, rewetting peatland, and increasing woodland by 50%. Water companies would be nationalised. Harmful pesticides including glyphosate would be phased out.

## Education
Proposals include £8bn additional school funding, £2.5bn annually for building repairs, abolishing Ofsted, ending academies, removing private school charitable status, scrapping university tuition fees, and restoring maintenance grants.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with railways returning to public ownership. Investment of £2.5bn annually in cycling and walking infrastructure is proposed. Free bus travel for under-18s, a frequent-flyer levy, and banning domestic flights where train journeys take under three hours are included.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The party would end the hostile environment, create safe asylum routes, abolish No Recourse to Public Funds conditions, end immigration detention except for public safety, and remove minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## Foreign Policy
The manifesto calls for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, cancelling Trident, and increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI.
